The test image shows a tomato **leaf** with multiple dark brown-black irregular ring-spot lesions scattered across the surface. The lesions appear as dark necrotic rings/circles with somewhat blurred margins, and the surrounding tissue remains green. This ring-spot pattern with blurred margins strongly suggests **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus**.

Now I'll view one reference image to confirm.

The TSWV reference shows bronzing with small scattered necrotic spots. The test image shows more prominent dark ring-spot lesions, but this is consistent with TSWV progression — the virus is known to produce distinct necrotic ring spots with blurred margins on leaves, and the ring patterns visible in the test image (dark circular/oval necrotic rings on green tissue) match the TSWV description: "distinct necrotic spots," "concentric ring patterns," and "blurred margins" that distinguish it from other leaf diseases.
